note: Out-of-pattern items surfaced ahead of the board. Both are illustrative. Branch identifiers are generic on purpose — ESFCU's 13 Maryland branches are public, but attributing a deposit outflow to a named branch would be inventing a fact about a real location.
source: Governance & Lineage Layer · Core Banking · Branch Deposit Data

items.title: Nightly refresh stalled — Howard University division
items.description: The nightly mapping job for the Howard University division failed to complete on two occasions this month. This is why the division reconciliation is pending. It is the silent kind of gap that used to surface only at month-end, when a figure looked wrong and nobody could say why.
items.detail: Stalled on the nights of 3 and 9 February. The job exits without raising an alert, so the enterprise warehouse simply carries a stale division balance rather than reporting a failure.
items.metric_text: 2 failures this month · last stall 9 Feb
items.policy_note: Not a policy breach — a data-integrity gap that would become one if the consolidated figure were cited unreconciled.

items.title: Branch deposit figure breaking its own trend
items.description: One branch shows a share balance that breaks its own trend by enough to warrant a look — a drop well outside its normal fortnightly range. The pattern reads as a single large member outflow rather than a data error, but it is the kind of thing you want to see before the board does.
items.detail: Branch 07. Share balance fell $4.2M over eleven days against a typical fortnightly range of ±$0.6M. No corresponding loan activity, and the source feed loaded cleanly, which is what points at a real outflow rather than a bad extract.
items.policy_note: Not a policy breach — concentration remains inside limits even with the outflow.
